before_step.derivation: From step 1, each bit is read once and maps the current state deterministically via F_0 or F_1; the bits do not otherwise interact. The given says the twelve input bits are independent, with each bit being 1 with probability 3/5 and 0 with probability 2/5. For any fixed length-12 string that has exactly seven 1s and five 0s, its probability factorizes over the twelve positions as a product of the per-bit probabilities: seven positions contribute a factor 3/5 for input 1, and five positions contribute a factor 2/5 for input 0. Multiplication is commutative, so the order of these factors does not matter; hence the probability is (3/5)^7(2/5)^5 regardless of which five positions carry the 0s or which seven carry the 1s. The deterministic state transitions do not alter the probability of a fixed input string, since the bits are the only random inputs. Thus every fixed length-12 string with exactly seven 1s has the same probability (3/5)^7(2/5)^5.
